question: An object is thrown vertically upwards with velocity u . Under the influence of gravity, the acceleration:

options.text: acts in the direction of motion
becomes zero at the highest point
acts opposite to the direction of motion

solution:
The correct answer is __**acts opposite to the direction of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When an object is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity **u**, it moves against the force of gravity. The acceleration due to gravity (**g**) always acts downward, i.e., opposite to the direction of motion during the upward journey. ***Hence, the correct statement is that acceleration acts opposite to the direction of motion.***
 
• As the object rises, the velocity decreases uniformly because the acceleration due to gravity **retards the upward motion**. At the highest point, the velocity of the object becomes zero momentarily, but the acceleration due to gravity still acts downward. *Hence, the statement "becomes zero at the highest point" is incorrect for acceleration.*
 
• During the entire motion, the acceleration due to gravity remains constant in magnitude and direction (downward). It does not act in the direction of motion during the upward journey. *This makes the statement "acts in the direction of motion" incorrect.*
